title: Perf benchmarking sync 2026-05-26
content:
Meeting: Performance & Benchmarking sync
Date: 2026-05-26
Attendees: Asha (chair), Ethan, Sofia, Rajesh, Maya, + SRE on call

Summary:
- Quick status: baseline harness runs finished this morning across A100/H100 pools. Raw numbers show a small regression on p95 latency for long-sequence (2k tokens) workloads on H100 with model redwood-1.0-13b-8bit.
- Throughput steady for short sequences (<=128) but 5-8% lower tokens/sec on medium batches (batch=8, seq=512) compared to last week's runs.
- Repro steps agreed and investigations assigned.

Recent test runs (high-level):
- run id: 2026-05-26-0900 (A100, redwood-1.0-13b, 8bit, batch sizes 1/4/8, seq 128/512/2048)
  - p50: 32ms (seq128, batch1)
  - p95: 210ms (seq2048, batch8) -> +12% vs baseline (2026-05-19)
  - throughput: 18.4k tokens/sec (seq128, batch8) -> on-par
- run id: 2026-05-26-1000 (H100, same config)
  - p50: 28ms (seq128, batch1)
  - p95: 260ms (seq2048, batch8) -> +22% vs baseline
  - throughput: 16.9k tokens/sec (seq512, batch8) -> -7% vs baseline
- KV-cache hit tests: when KV cache hit ratio >85% we still see ~4% p95 regression on H100 runs.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel selection change in runtime v0.37.2 (recent PR merged last week) picks a different matmul kernel for certain layer sizes on H100 leading to tail latency variance. (Ethan taking lead)
2) Autoscaling/placement policy now co-locates inference pods with different memory pressure, causing noisy neighbors for medium batch runs (SRE/Sofia investigating placement logs).
3) Minor change in batching logic (continuous batching threshold tweak) increased worst-case queueing for long sequences (Rajesh to validate with microbench).

Immediate reproduction plan (concrete steps):
- Ethan: run targeted microbench that pins the kernel selection path and toggles the backend flag (USE_NEW_KERNEL=0/1). Compare p95 and perf counters. Command: ./bench/run_bench.sh --model redwood-1.0-13b --device h100 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --repeat 10. Due: 2026-05-27 EOD.
- Sofia + SRE: collect pod placement and GPU utilization traces for the failing runs (logs in gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-26/placement/). Look for co-located non-inference workloads. Due: 2026-05-28.
- Rajesh: run micro-batching harness with continuous-batcher off to confirm queueing hypothesis. Add histogram of queued-request times. Due: 2026-05-27 noon.
- Maya: rerun full harness on a clean H100 fleet (no other tenants) to see if regression persists. If clean fleet passes, point toward noisy neighbors. Due: 2026-05-27 morning.

Notes from discussion:
- We confirmed the regression is most visible at high sequence lengths (>=1024) and medium batch sizes (4-8). Short sequences and single-token inference unaffected.
- No change in model weights or tokenizer between runs; this looks infra/runtime-related.
- Telemetry: need to capture per-layer kernel id and per-invocation CUDA stream metrics for the next runs. Add to bench harness logs. (Ethan to update bench harness)
- We don't have a perf regression alert threshold for p95 > 10% for long-seq runs; agreed to add alert in Datadog next week. (Asha to create ticket)

Action items (owner -> task -> due):
- Ethan Liu -> run kernel toggle microbench & upload perf counters to gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-27/ (due 2026-05-27)
- Sofia Martinez -> placement logs + SRE coordination (create RSRV ticket, due 2026-05-28)
- Rajesh Singh -> microbench with continuous-batcher off, produce queue histograms (due 2026-05-27)
- Maya Chen -> clean-fleet harness runs and baseline comparison (due 2026-05-27)
- Asha Patel -> create Datadog alert + tracker ticket (RSRV-742) and follow up with product on customer impact messaging (due 2026-05-28)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- If kernel toggle fixes p95 but reduces throughput, is that acceptable? We need to measure unit cost delta (tokens/$). Product/Cost team input required. (Product contact: Nikhil)
- If noisy neighbors are root cause, SRE may need to update placement policy or enforce stricter isolation for Dedicated fleets. Estimate impact on capacity planning.
- Should we temporarily pin runtime to v0.37.1 for critical fleets until fix verified? (Tentative emergency rollback plan prepared if regression >20% for >=2 customers)

Quick links:
- Full harness results: gs://redwood-benchmarks/2026-05-26/results.csv
- Bench harness PR for kernel selection flags: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Tracker ticket: RSRV-742 (perf-regression-long-seq)

Next meeting: 2026-05-28 10:00 PT (quick sync to review reproduction results)

Notes to self / informal:
- keep runs deterministic: set SEED=42, disable background uploads.
- remind bench infra to rotate logs daily to avoid hitting storage quotas.
- record the exact commit hashes used for each run in future (slot in bench metadata).

-- end of notes --
